Chapter 3 116
4
Microsoft Entra Domain Services
In the last few years, we have seen a major shift to cloud services. However, many
organizations still have a significant portion of their infrastructure on premises. While
Microsoft Entra provides identity and access management services in the cloud, some
organizations idx_e34c3c97 still rely on Active Directory services like domain join, group policy, and
Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP)/ Kerberos authentication. Microsoft Entra
Domain Services provides managed domain idx_da42f87c services in the cloud to organizations with such
requirements. It enables organizations to use familiar Active Directory features without
deploying, managing, or patching domain controllers. This is especially useful for scenarios
where an organization wants to reduce its on-premises footprint, but a hybrid identity solution
is necessary to support both on-premises and cloud resources. Using this solution,
organizations can migrate legacy, directory-dependent applications to the cloud with minimal
redevelopment. This chapter will cover:
Introduction to Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Common deployment scenarios
Deploying Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Administering Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Securing Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Cloud-based directory services
As organizations increasingly transition their workloads to the cloud, the need for legacy
support remains, particularly for applications and resources that depend on directory services
like domain join, LDAP, Kerberos authentication, and group policy. Microsoft offers two ways
that provide idx_6b04e71e traditional Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) in the cloud.
•
•
•
•
•
Self-managed domain
A self-managed domain can be idx_2c69a4d5 created using resources like Virtual Machines (VMs),
Windows idx_3aa531bf Server, and AD DS. This is like installing and maintaining a traditional AD DS
environment in the cloud. Instead of physical servers, it is installed on VMs in the cloud. The
organization is responsible for managing, patching, and idx_a100505a securing the Domain Controllers
(DCs) and related infrastructure. Common deployment models for using a self-managed AD
DS environment include:
Standalone cloud-only AD DS: This is a completely independent AD DS environment
and does not integrate with an on-premises AD DS environment. This is useful for
organizations that would like to lift and shift their on-premises AD DS infrastructure to
the cloud.
Extend on-premises domain to Azure: In this approach, the on-premises Active
Directory Domain Services (AD DS) domain is extended into Azure by establishing
connectivity between an Azure virtual network and the on-premises network through
either a VPN or an ExpressRoute connection. Azure virtual machines are then joined to

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 3 116
chunks.content:
this virtual network, enabling them to participate in and authenticate against the on-
premises AD DS environment. Azure VMs can also be promoted as additional DCs that
replicate over the VPN or ExpressRoute connection.
While this may be a quick and viable option for some organizations, they still retain the
overhead and management of the servers running the domain controllers. A managed domain
solves this problem as explained in the next section.
Overview of Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Microsoft Entra Domain Services offers a seamless way to extend Active Directory
capabilities to the cloud idx_f4d9e4f6 without the operational overhead of deploying, managing, or patching
VMs. By integrating with Microsoft Entra ID, it enables organizations to create a hybrid
identity infrastructure that supports both legacy and cloud-native applications, fostering
modernization and flexibility. Domain Services offers a smaller subset of features as compared
to self-managed domain, thereby reducing complexity. For example, there are no AD forests,
domain sites, or replication links to manage.
With this managed service, businesses can migrate directory-dependent workloads to the
cloud more efficiently, minimizing redevelopment and ensuring continuity for critical systems.
Entra Domain Services also helps improve security posture by leveraging cloud-based updates
and monitoring, reducing the risks associated with on-premises infrastructure. It is ideal for
organizations looking to reduce their on-premises footprint while maintaining compatibility
with established authentication and policy management tools. As enterprises embrace cloud-
•
•

first strategies, Microsoft Entra Domain Services plays a vital role in simplifying identity
management and accelerating digital transformation.
A Domain Services managed domain lets idx_731ebd00 organizations run legacy applications that cannot
use modern authentication in the cloud. Using Domain Services managed domain,
organizations can lift and shift these legacy applications idx_833df48c to the cloud without having to
manage an extensive Active Directory environment in the cloud.

This chapter will focus on Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain. Let's dive
deeper.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services managed domain
When existing workloads are migrated to the cloud, directory-dependent applications use
LDAP for idx_225bec38 read and write access to AD DS directory. Applications that run on Windows Server
are normally deployed on domain joined VMs so that they can be joined to the AD DS domain
and managed using Group Policy. To authenticate idx_2174d153 users, these applications use Kerberos or NT
LAN Manager (NTLM) authentication.
Organizations use one of the following ways to migrate such workloads to the cloud:
Configure a idx_aafd67ec site-to-site Virtual Private Network (VPN) connection between Azure
workloads and on-premises AD DS environments to enable on-premises DCs to
provide authentication services via VPN.
Create replica DCs in Azure VMs to extend the on-premises domain to the cloud.
Authentication is provided by these DCs. They replicate directory information from the
on-premises DCs.
Deploy a stand-alone AD DS environment in Azure using DCs that run on Azure VMs.
This is a completely separate AD DS environment and information is not replicated
from on-premises AD DS.
In all these approaches, VPN connections become a bottleneck which are vulnerable to
network glitches and outages. Domain Services provides an alternative approach to reduce
complexity and increase reliability to create an integrated identity solution for both hybrid and
cloud-only environments.

Microsoft Entra Domain Services for hybrid organizations: Organizations that run a
hybrid infrastructure where the on-premises AD DS environment is synchronized with
Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft Entra Connect.
Microsoft Entra Domain Services for cloud-only organizations: Organizations that
don't have an on-premises AD DS environment and whose identities are completely
managed in the cloud.

chunks.content:
Chapter 4 120
To get started, organizations must first create a Domain Services managed domain by defining
a unique namespace, which serves as the domain name, such as mydomainservices.com.
Basic concepts
Before we idx_d6f1caad proceed with creating a managed domain, let's understand some important
concepts as there are some differences in how Domain Services behaves in comparison to an
on-premises AD DS environment.
Replica sets
When a managed domain is provisioned, Azure automatically deploys two Windows DCs
within the idx_0d333c15 selected Azure region. This deployment, referred to as a replica set, provides
redundancy and high availability for the managed domain. A key advantage of using a
managed domain is that organizations are relieved of the responsibility for maintaining these
domain controllers, as Azure fully manages them as part of the service. This management
includes built-in features such as automated backups and encryption of data at rest, ensuring
both operational resilience and security compliance.
Managed domains can be expanded to include more than one replica set per Microsoft Entra
tenant. Replica sets can be added to any peered virtual network in any Azure region. This
provides geographical disaster recovery in case an Azure region becomes unavailable. All
replica sets share the same namespace and configuration and contain the same data. Any
changes, such as configuration, user identity, groups, or Group Policy objects are applied to all
replica sets using AD DS replication.
Each replica set is created in a virtual network that must be peered with every other virtual
network containing a replica set. A single virtual network can host multiple replica sets if each
one resides in a different subnet. You can create up to five replica sets per managed domain.
Forests and trusts
Forest is a logical idx_a6f4144e unit in Active Directory that can contain one or more domains. User objects,
groups, and devices are stored in domains. Domains also provide authentication services. In
Domain Services, a forest can contain only one domain.
A forest trust can be created with another domain to allow users access to resources.
Depending on requirements, the following types of trusts can be created:
Two-way: Users in both domains can access each other's resources. •
121 Microsoft Entra Domain Services
One-way outgoing: Users in the on-premises domain access resources in the managed
domain but users in the managed domain cannot access resources in the on-premises
domain.
One-way incoming: Users in the managed domain can access resources in the on-
premises idx_f86e55c3 domain but users in the on-premises domain cannot access resources in the
managed domain.
Synchronization
An automatic one-way synchronization is configured from Microsoft Entra ID to a managed

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 4 120
chunks.content:
domain. This means that resources idx_0d3ad66a created in Microsoft Entra ID are synchronized to the
managed domain, but the resources created in the managed domain are not synchronized to
Microsoft Entra ID. Applications and services in the Azure environment connected to the
managed domain can take advantage of features like domain join, group policy, LDAP, and
Kerberos.
If organizations have a hybrid environment with on-premises AD that is connected to
Microsoft Entra ID using Microsoft Entra Connect, resources from on-premises AD are
synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID and from there they are automatically synchronized to the
managed domain. The following figure shows this:
Figure 4.1: Replication in a hybrid environment
The initial synchronization may take a few days to complete depending on the number of
objects to be synchronized. After the initial synchronization is complete, changes made in
Microsoft Entra ID are automatically synchronized to Domain Services.
It is possible to scope user synchronization to only the users that originated in the cloud. This
way users from the on-premises AD DS environment will not be synchronized to the managed
domain.
Domain management
A managed domain is a DNS namespace and directory. The DCs that contain all resources like
users idx_896e061f and groups are part of the managed service and users cannot sign in to these DCs. A VM
•
•

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 4 122
chunks.content:
Chapter 4 122
is created that is joined to the managed domain. All domain management tools such as AD
Administrative Center, Group Policy objects, and DNS snap-ins are installed on this VM and
used to perform all administrative tasks. A managed domain is largely read-only.
Administrators idx_77129325 can create custom Organizational Units (OUs) with the managed domain but
cannot make changes to user attributes, passwords, or group memberships.
While creating a managed domain, you will be asked to specify a DNS domain name. There
are some considerations when choosing a domain name as described below:
Built-in domain name: By default, the managed domain is assigned a name with
the .onmicrosoft.com suffix. This default naming convention is not recommended
when planning to use secure LDAP for internet-based access to the managed domain.
Because Microsoft retains ownership of the .onmicrosoft.com namespace,
organizations cannot obtain a publicly trusted digital certificate for this domain. As a
result, Certificate Authorities (CAs) will not issue a certificate to secure LDAP
connections using the default domain name.
Custom domain names: It is recommended to use a custom domain that the
organization owns and is routable.
Non-routable domain suffixes: It is not recommended to use a non-routable domain
name such as litware.local. Because these domains are not routable, they can cause
issues with DNS resolution.
The following DNS name restrictions apply:
Managed domain names cannot contain a prefix that is longer than 15 characters.
The name should be unique in your virtual network. The following scenarios could
cause a conflict:
If you have an AD domain with the same DNS domain name on the Azure virtual
network.
If the virtual network on which you plan to enable the managed domain is
connected to your on-premises AD domain via VPN, make sure that the on-
premises network does not have a domain with the same DNS domain name.
If you have an existing Azure cloud service with the same name on the virtual
network.
Consider all the above points to accurately create your domain before synchronizing users from
Active Directory.
•
•
•
•
•
◦
◦
◦
123 Microsoft Entra Domain Services
User account creation
User idx_ed0ea6b0 accounts are synchronized from the connected Microsoft Entra ID tenant which can also
include accounts synchronized from any on-premises AD DS environment. Users can also be
created directly in the managed domain. However, these users will not be synchronized back to
Microsoft Entra ID.
Password policy
Domain idx_3743c07a Services has its own default password policy that includes settings for account
lockout, maximum password age, and password complexity. Policies are distributed through
group association.
Account lockout policy applies to all users in the managed domain regardless of how they were

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid
chunks.heading: Chapter 4 122
chunks.content:
created. The following settings apply:
Account lockout duration: 30 minutes
Number of failed logon attempts allowed: 5
Reset failed login attempts count after: 2 minutes
Maximum password age: 90 days
Account lockouts only occur within the managed domain and only due to failed sign-in
attempts against resources within the managed domain. Users who are synchronized from
Microsoft Entra ID are not locked out in their source directory.
Other policies like password length and password complexity apply only to the users created
directly in the managed domain. The following settings apply:
Minimum password length: 7 characters
Passwords must meet complexity requirements
The account lockout or password settings in the default policy cannot be modified.
Administrators can create their own custom password policies and configure them to override
the default password policy. The custom policies can be scoped to user groups.

Enabling user accounts for Domain Services
Domain Services needs password hashes in a format that is suitable for NTLM and Kerberos
authentication. Microsoft Entra ID does not generate or store password hashes in this format
until Domain idx_3cab2e33 Services is enabled in the tenant. Cloud-only users must change their passwords

synchronization of password hashes must be enabled in Microsoft Entra Connect settings.

domain is deleted, all associated password hashes are permanently removed. Credential
information synchronized in Entra ID cannot be reused when provisioning another managed
domain. Microsoft Entra ID must generate and store fresh password hashes in the newly
created managed domain.

Creating a forest trust
A trust relationship idx_0d687870 can be created between a managed domain and an idx_2ec8223e on-premises AD DS
environment. This trust enables users, applications, and devices from a managed domain to
authenticate against an on-premises domain and vice versa. A forest trust helps users access
resources in environments where password hashes cannot be synchronized or in passwordless
scenarios such as smart cards. It also enables access in hybrid environments that require access
to on-premises environments.
To enable forest trust, the following prerequisites must be met:
An active Azure subscription with a Microsoft Entra tenant associated. The Entra
tenant idx_a6c272a1 could be cloud-only or synchronized with an on-premises domain.
A Domain Services managed domain configured with a custom DNS and a valid SSL
certificate.
An on-premises domain that is reachable either via ExpressRoute or VPN connectivity.
The network must meet the following requirements:
Any firewall ports and DCs must allow traffic that is necessary to create a trust.
All DCs that need to have a trust with the managed domain must have these
ports open.
Use static private IP addresses.
Avoid overlapping IP address spaces to ensure successful communication
between Azure and on-premises.
Domain Services must have its own subnet.
Peered virtual networks should not be transitive.
Ensure continuous connectivity and DNS name resolution between Azure and
on-premises.
An account with Application Administrator and Groups Administrator role
assigned.
A Domain Administrator account for the on-premises domain.

Now that idx_21a324b0 we have learned how to create and configure a managed domain, let's learn some
basic administration tasks.
Creating an administrator VM
To administer a managed domain, you need to have a management machine. This is usually a
Windows idx_ec54da92 Server VM joined to the managed domain. You can either domain-join an existing
Windows Server VM running in Azure or create a new Windows Server VM in Azure and join it
to the managed domain. The following are the high-level steps:
Create a Windows Server VM in Azure and add it to the managed domain. 1.

Creating an OU
OUs in an idx_1ec3ba69 AD DS environment let you logically group user accounts, service accounts, and
computer accounts. Specific administrators and group policies can then be assigned to specific
OUs. In a managed domain, the following two built-in OUs exist:
AADDC Computers: This container stores the computer objects for all computers that
are joined to the managed domain.
AADDC Users: This container stores the users and groups synchronized from the
Microsoft Entra tenant.
OUs created in a hybrid on-premises AD DS domain are not synchronized to the managed
domain. Instead, managed domains maintain a flat OU hierarchy, and all user accounts
synchronized from the on-premises AD DS environment are placed in the AADDC Users OU.
Administrators can create custom OUs in the managed domain to meet the specific needs of
their organization.
Before creating an OU, the following prerequisites must be met:
An active Azure subscription with a Microsoft Entra tenant associated. The Entra
tenant could either be cloud-only or synchronized with an on-premises domain.
A management VM running Windows Server, joined to the managed domain.
A user account in the Microsoft Entra tenant with membership of the Microsoft Entra
DC administrators group.
There are idx_7b2e8e44 some limitations and considerations when creating a custom OU in a managed
domain. They are as follows:
Use a user account with membership in the AAD DC administrators group to create an
OU.
The steps to create a Windows Server VM in Azure are beyond the scope of this
book. The steps to add a Windows Server VM to a managed domain are the
same as adding it to an on-premises AD DS domain.

Users and groups created in the custom OU are not available in the Microsoft Entra

Administering GPOs
In AD, settings for users and computer objects are configured and managed through GPOs.
Domain Services idx_f052c6c5 includes built-in GPOs for the AADDC Users and AADDC Computers OUs.
Administrators can customize the settings in these GPOs to suit their organization's

Managing DNS
Domain Services incorporates an integrated DNS server that delivers name resolution services

to the managed domain, DNS records may need to be created to provide name resolution for
these services. Members of the AAD DC administrators group can create and edit DNS records
in the managed domain.
In a hybrid environment, DNS information configured in the on-premises AD domain is not
synchronized to the managed domain. To resolve resources in the managed domain,
conditional forwarders need to be created that point to DNS servers in the environment.

Securing Domain Services
The following idx_1702dc72 section explains some of the key security settings that must be enabled to secure
your Domain Services managed domain.
Securing managed domain
Microsoft Entra Domain Services allows the use of NTLM v1 and TLS v1 by default. These
ciphers idx_e130d42b may be required for some legacy applications to run, but they are considered insecure
and weak and must be disabled if there are no applications that need them. Microsoft is
deprecating the use of TLS 1.0 and TLS 1.1. TLS 1.2 and later versions offer improved security
features such as perfect forward secrecy and stronger cipher suites.
To manage security settings for the managed domain, follow the steps below:
Sign in to https://entra.microsoft.com as a Global Administrator.
Navigate to Entra ID | Domain services. In the right pane, click on the managed
domain name.

chunks.title: masteringmicrosoftentraid

1.2 141 Microsoft Entra Domain Services
Click on Security settings. Click on Enable or Disable for the following settings:
TLS 1.2 Only Mode: Before enabling TLS 1.2 only mode, ensure that there are no
applications that still use earlier versions of TLS.
NTLM v1 Authentication: If this mode is enabled, all NTLM v1 requests will fail.
Password synchronization from On-premises: If this setting is disabled, on-
premises user accounts will not be able to authenticate in the managed domain.
NTLM Password Synchronization: If this setting is disabled, synchronized user
idx_c80033f5 accounts will not be able to use NTLM authentication in the managed domain.
Kerberos RC4 Encryption: If this is disabled, all Kerberos requests that use RC4
encryption will fail.
Kerberos Armoring: Enabling this setting will provide a secure channel between
Kerberos client and the Kerberos Distribution Center (KDC).
LDAP Signing: Enabling this setting will require all LDAP clients to request
signing during bind time.
LDAP Channel Binding: Enabling this setting will require all LDAP clients to
provide channel binding information while communicating with the directory.
Once done, click Save.
Carefully consider the NTLM and TLS requirements for your organization and configure them
appropriately to ensure that applications continue to work without compromising security.
Configuring Kerberos constrained delegation
Some applications need to access resources in the context of a different user. AD DS supports a
idx_d2874284 mechanism called Kerberos delegation that lets one account impersonate another account to
access resources. For idx_4f53fd6d example, a website can impersonate another user to access back-end
resources. Kerberos delegation is considered idx_52a84546 insecure because it does not restrict which
resources an impersonating account can access. In contrast, Kerberos Constrained
Delegation (KCD) allows administrators to explicitly define the resources that can be accessed
on behalf of another user. Configuring KCD requires domain administrator privileges to enable
a domain account for a specific service, and the delegated account is limited to operating
within a single domain. A managed domain does not give Domain Administrator privileges, so
account-based KCD cannot be used. Domain Services managed domains use a more secure
resource-based KCD, available in Windows Server 2012 and later. This capability enables
administrators to configure constrained delegation for their services. Using resource-based
KCD, back-end service administrators can explicitly allow or deny specific front-end services
from performing delegation, thereby providing finer grained control over authentication flows.

$ImpersonatingAccount = Get-ADComputer -Identity contoso-
webapp.aaddscontoso.com

PrincipalsAllowedToDelegateToAccount $ImpersonatingAccount
To configure resource-based KCD for user account, use the following PowerShell
command:
$ImpersonatingAccount = Get-ADUser -Identity appsvc

$ImpersonatingAccount

DC Computers or Microsoft Entra DC Users containers.

You must be a member of the Microsoft Entra DC administrators group to run the

Configuring Kerberos constrained delegation allows a service to securely act on behalf of a user
only to specific permitted services, limiting impersonation scope and reducing lateral-
movement risk.

Summary
This chapter covers how organizations with dependency on legacy methods like LDAP and
Kerberos can seamlessly transition to the cloud. It explained how organizations can use
Microsoft Entra Domain Services to provide these capabilities in the cloud with minimum
administrative overhead. It began by explaining the difference between a self-managed
domain and a managed domain. It then went deep into managed domains outlining the basic
concepts required for creating and managing a managed domain. It explained how to create,
manage and administer a managed domain. In the next chapter, we will learn about Security
Copilot in Microsoft Entra.

AI in Microsoft Entra
The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in idx_8573a8c0 cybersecurity has revolutionized how
organizations approach the protection of their digital assets. AI systems can analyze vast
amounts of data at speeds that far surpass human capabilities, allowing for the rapid
identification of potential threats and vulnerabilities. Machine learning algorithms, for
instance, can detect unusual patterns of behavior that may indicate a cyber-attack, such as
unauthorized access, phishing attempts, or malware infections. By continuously learning from
new data, these systems become increasingly adept at recognizing both known and emerging
threats, reducing the window of opportunity for malicious actors.
Moreover, AI-powered tools can automate routine security tasks, such as monitoring network
traffic, updating access controls, and responding to incidents. This not only improves the
efficiency of cybersecurity operations but also frees human experts to focus on more complex
challenges. In environments like Microsoft Entra, solutions such as Security Copilot leverage AI
to provide actionable insights, streamline investigations, and enhance overall security posture.
This chapter will cover the following topics:
Overview of Microsoft Security Copilot
Security Copilot in Microsoft Entra
Security Copilot agents in Microsoft Entra
Microsoft Entra Agent ID
Microsoft Security Copilot
Microsoft Security idx_670d9174 Copilot is an advanced, AI-driven cybersecurity solution designed to
empower security teams with intelligent insights and faster response capabilities. By
leveraging the power of generative AI and deep integration with Microsoft's security
ecosystem, Security Copilot helps organizations identify, investigate, and remediate threats
•
•
•
•
with unprecedented speed and accuracy. It acts as a virtual assistant for security professionals,
automating routine tasks such as incident triage, alert prioritization, and threat hunting,
thereby freeing up valuable time for analysts to focus on strategic initiatives.
Security Copilot integrates seamlessly with platforms like Microsoft Entra, Microsoft Defender
XDR, Microsoft Intune, and non-Microsoft services like Jamf and Red Canary allowing it to
access and analyze data across a wide range of environments. It continuously learns from new
threat intelligence and user feedback, adapting to emerging risks and evolving tactics
employed by malicious actors. The solution presents findings in clear, actionable formats,
enabling teams to understand complex threat scenarios and make informed decisions quickly.
Additionally, Security Copilot enhances collaboration by providing guided investigation
workflows, recommended remediation steps, and detailed reporting, making it an essential
tool for modern security operations centers.

Privacy and data security
Microsoft Security idx_c5eeb5b6 Copilot stores and processes Customer Data and system-generated logs
as part of the service.
Microsoft defines Customer Data as all data such as text, sound, video, image file, and software
that are provided to Microsoft by the customer through the use of its online services. It does
not include information used to configure the service, such as settings or names of resources.
In Security Copilot, Customer Data includes user submitted prompts, information retrieved to
generate responses, responses, and file uploads.
When customers use Microsoft online services, system-generated logs are created as part of
service operations. These logs record system activity over time so that Microsoft can monitor
whether the service is operating as expected. The storage and processing of these logs are
essential to identify and respond to policy violations and fraud. This also aids in optimizing
system, network, and application performance, helps with security investigations, and ensures
compliance with laws and regulations. System-generated logs include account information
such as tenant ID, account ID, and licensing details, as well as usage and performance data and
internal system behavior information.
153 AI in Microsoft Entra
By default, data sharing is turned on. This can be changed by Global Administrators and
Security Administrators who have the Capacity Contributor role. This data is only used by
Microsoft to improve product performance. It is not used to train Azure OpenAI models, shared
with OpenAI or third parties, nor is it used for sales.
Security Copilot integrates with other Microsoft 365 and Microsoft security services that an
organization is licensed to use. Organizations have the option to allow users to query
information from those services both in the embedded and standalone experiences.
Data storage locations
Data is stored in the location idx_32fcd684 you select when you onboard to Security Copilot. Once this
selection is made, the data storage location cannot be changed. If data sharing is enabled,
Customer Data (except uploaded files) may be stored outside of the chosen workspace
location. Uploaded files remain in the chosen workspace location. If content from an uploaded
file is part of the response, that content may be stored outside the chosen workspace location.
Uploaded files are only available to the user who uploaded them.
Data retention
Customer Data is stored idx_57d65126 in the organization's tenant for as long as the organization has an
active Security Copilot subscription. It is deleted within 180 days if the organization deletes all

Chapter 5 154
usage is measured in terms of Security Compute Units (SCUs). These idx_a2b91313 are the compute
resources that are needed for Security Copilot to work. Security Copilot works on provisioned
capacity and overage capacity. Provisioned capacity is billed idx_37663193 by the hour, whereas overage
capacity is billed idx_36e20c15 usage. SCUs can be provisioned flexibly to accommodate regular and peak
workload. To handle unexpected workload spikes, overage capacity can be provisioned that
makes additional SCUs available when the originally provisioned ones are used during
unexpected workload spikes. The overage units are billed on demand and can be set to
unlimited or be capped at a maximum amount. SCUs are billed on hourly blocks and have a
minimum of one hour. Let's understand this with the help of an example.
Let's assume that an organization has one SCU provisioned with no overage. If this one SCU
gets consumed within 45 minutes, Security Copilot will not process further prompts till the
hour is reset. If the organization now provisions an additional SCU as overage and the
provisioned SCU gets consumed within 45 minutes, the overage SCU will be used, and Security
Copilot will continue to process requests. If the provisioned SCU does not get consumed within
the hour, the overage SCU is not used, and the organization is not charged for it.
Prerequisites
To get started with idx_9fa26978 Security Copilot, ensure that the following prerequisites are met:
An Azure subscription with Azure Owner or Contributor role
At least 1 SCU is required for non M365 E5 or E7 customers
It is recommended to use roles with fewest permissions to improve security for your
organization. Other idx_dfb6b7f0 supported roles include but are not limited to Billing Admin, Intune
Admin, Entra Compliance Admin.
